lede: The week's most consequential meeting is Mountain Village Town Council on Thursday, where a resolution setting an appreciation cap on deed-restricted units will determine how well the affordable housing stock actually holds its value over time — that's a real decision with long-term consequences for workforce housing. Ouray County Planning Commission also holds three public hearings Wednesday, including a full repeal of Section 16 of their land use code, and Telluride's P&Z takes up the school district's employee housing proposal and a short-term rental code amendment the same evening. School starts Tuesday for Telluride R-1 kids, and the Oak Street Park SummerSHOW wraps the week Thursday with a free Deltaphonic set.
